summary: Dodrupchen Rinpoche (1927–2022) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under teachers including Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Kunzang Pelden, and taught students such as Ronald M. Davidson, Tulku Thondup, and Tulku Hungkar Dorje.

Domenico Pezzi (1844–1905) was a linguist and Indologist. He earned his Ph.D. under Giovanni Flechia at the University of Turin (~1861–1865), where he later served in multiple faculty posts, ultimately succeeding Flechia as ordinary professor in 1891.

Dominic Goodall is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He completed a D.Phil. at Oxford (1995) under Alexis Sanderson and studied with Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan. His career includes posts at Oxford, the École française d'Extrême-Orient, and EPHE.

Dominic Sur is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Harvard and the University of Virginia, completing doctoral work under David Germano alongside Karen Christina Lang, Kurtis R. Schaeffer, and Khenpo Lama Chönam. He joined Utah State University (attested 2017).

Dominik Haas is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He completed his doctorate under Marion Rastelli at the University of Vienna (2018–2022), where he also worked and lectured, before holding positions at the Austrian Academy of Sciences and IIAS in 2024.

Dominik Schröder (1910–1974) was an anthropologist in Iranian and Central Asian studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Fu Jen (M.A. 1945) and Frankfurt (Ph.D. ~1949–1951), and held posts at the Anthropos Institute and Nanzan University (1960–1969).

Dominik Wujastyk is an Indologist who completed a DPhil at the University of Oxford (1978–1982). He held long-term posts at the Wellcome Institute (~1985–2002), UCL (2002–2009), the University of Vienna (2009–2014), and the University of Alberta (2015–2024).

Dominique Sportiche is a linguist who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (~1978–1984). He held a post at the University of California, Los Angeles (~1988), and taught Edward Garrett.

Dominique-Sila Khan (1949–2016) was a scholar in Indology and religious studies who studied at Paris-Sorbonne University. She served as a Research Fellow at the Institute of Rajasthan Studies (attested 2000).
Don A. Pittman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He was a doctoral candidate at the University of Chicago and served on the faculty at Texas Christian University.

Don Handelman is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at McGill (~1956–1960), Pittsburgh (~1960–1963), and Manchester (~1966–1969), and served as Professor of Anthropology at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1972–2007).

Don Martino de Zilva Wickremasinghe (1865–1937) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Erlangen-Nuremberg under Wilhelm Geiger and George Uglow Pope. He served as epigraphist for the Government of Ceylon (~1899–1929) and at the University of London (~1918–1928).

Donald A. Ringe is a linguist and Indologist. He earned an M.Phil. at Oxford and a PhD at Yale under Warren Crawford Cowgill. After teaching at Bard College, he joined the linguistics faculty at the University of Pennsylvania in 1985.

Donald E. Gjertson is a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Stanford (~1970–1975) under John Ching-yu Wang and Akira Takeda, and held a post at the University of Massachusetts Amherst (~1976–2011).

Donald Eric Capps (1939–2015) was a religious studies scholar who earned degrees from Yale and Chicago (Ph.D. ~1970). He taught at Chicago, UNC Charlotte, and Phillips University before serving at Princeton Theological Seminary (1981–2009).
Donald Ferguson (1853–1910) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He was educated at Denmark Hill Grammar School, Regent's Park College, and University College London.

Donald Harper is a sinologist who taught Zhiru Shi. He held a post at the University of Arizona (attested 1999) and serves as Centennial Professor of Chinese Studies at the University of Chicago (attested 2026).

Donald K. Swearer is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who was mentored by Kenneth K. S. Ch'en and Singkha Wannasai. He held posts at Swarthmore College (~1970–1993), Chiang Mai University, and Harvard University (2004–2010).

Donald Keene (1922–2019) was a Japanologist who studied at Columbia and Harvard, learning under Wm. Theodore de Bary. He held posts at the University of Cambridge (1949–1954) and Columbia University (from 1955), and taught Royall Tyler.

Donald Phillip Verene is a philosopher who completed his doctorate at Washington University in St. Louis (~1959–1964) and studied at Knox College. He served as department chair at Emory University (1982–1988) and held visiting fellowships at Oxford and Rome.
